## Overview

BeyondBench is a dynamic evaluation framework that generates algorithmic problems to measure genuine reasoning ability in language models rather than memorized patterns. The paper was accepted at ICLR 2026.

## Problem Statement

Evaluating language models fairly is becoming harder as static benchmarks available on the internet risk contamination by training data, making it unclear whether models are truly reasoning or just recalling answers.

## Contamination Resistance Approach

The contamination resistance of BeyondBench rests on three guarantees: (i) the problem space is vastly larger than any static dataset, (ii) every instance has a unique, verifiable solution, and (iii) isomorphic transformations generate semantically equivalent but syntactically new problems.

## Framework Details

The framework covers 44 algorithmic tasks with 117 variations across three difficulty levels: the Easy Suite (29 tasks) for arithmetic and statistics, the Medium Suite (5 tasks, 49 variations) for sequence patterns and reasoning, and the Hard Suite (10 tasks, 68 variations) for NP-complete and constraint satisfaction problems. Each task draws from a space exceeding 10^15 unique instances, with deterministically verified solutions.

## Evaluation Results

101 language models were evaluated (85 open-source, 16 closed-source), spanning 0.5B to 141B parameters and multiple quantization schemes, using three-fold evaluation for robustness.

This paper presents a benchmark self-evolving framework to dynamically evaluate rapidly advancing Large Language Models (LLMs), and was published at COLING 2025.

The framework utilizes a multi-agent system to reframe new evolving instances with high confidence that extend existing benchmarks, implementing six reframing operations to construct evolving instances testing LLMs against diverse queries, shortcut biases and probing their problem-solving sub-abilities.

Experimental results show a performance decline in most LLMs against their original results under scalable and robust evaluations, offering a more accurate reflection of model capabilities alongside their fine-grained evaluation. The framework is intended to contribute to the research community for continuously evolving benchmarks alongside LLM development.

## Overview

EvolMathEval is an automated mathematical benchmark generation and evolution framework based on evolutionary testing.

## Purpose and Problem it Addresses

The rapid advancement of Large Language Models poses a significant challenge to existing mathematical reasoning benchmarks, as these benchmarks tend to become easier over time as LLMs can learn from the published benchmarks, which hinders the precise evaluation of the true capabilities of state-of-the-art models.

## Capabilities and Results

EvolMathEval can generate a large volume of high-difficulty problems through continuous self-iteration and can significantly enhance the complexity of public datasets like GSM8K through evolution, reducing model accuracy by an average of 48%.

When solving these evolved problems, LLMs tend to bypass complex multi-step logical reasoning by relying on simplistic and fuzzy conditions, leading to incorrect solutions—a phenomenon defined as the "Pseudo Aha Moment," which accounts for 77% to 100% of errors on targeted problems.

KBE-DME is designed to overcome the challenges of data contamination and data saturation through Dynamic Multimodal Evaluation via Knowledge-Enhanced Benchmark Evolution.

The approach represents multimodal tasks in the standard VQA (Visual Question Answering) format, modeling each problem using a Graph formulation with multimodal knowledge triplets, and extracting candidate multimodal knowledge triplets to identify key triplets necessary for answering questions.
